report.executive_summary: This memo independently recomputes eligibility, ranking and energy gaps for the four pump modules from the trusted table and the client policy, then audits the delivered proposal report against them. All four candidates pass both gates. P2 is the lowest-energy qualifying module at 12 kWh per common acceptance run, ahead of P3 (52 kWh), P1 (56 kWh) and P4 (58 kWh). Every figure I checked in the proposal matches the trusted source, and its recommendation P2 is client-correct. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability remain unverified and enter neither the audit nor this ruling. I cast my ballot for P2.
report.figure_caption: Verified energy per common acceptance run (kWh) for all four qualifying modules, with quality and defect values shown; the largest gap (40 kWh, P2 to P3) and both policy gates are annotated.

recommendation.rationale: Independently verified: P2 is the lowest-energy qualifying module at 12 kWh, 40 kWh below runner-up P3, with the highest quality index (97) and one raw defect, well inside both gates. No tie-break applies. My recomputation from the trusted table confirms the proposal's figures and its client-correct conclusion.

sections.body: Recomputing from the trusted table: quality indices are P1 84, P2 97, P3 80, P4 81 — all at or above the gate of 80, so all four pass. P3 sits exactly on the threshold with zero margin, which is a compliance fact worth recording, not a disqualifier. Raw defect counts are P1 4, P2 1, P3 3, P4 0 — all at or below the maximum of 5, so all four also pass. No candidate is near the defect ceiling. Eligibility therefore admits the full field, and the award turns entirely on measured energy.
sections.heading: Recomputed Eligibility Against Both Gates

sections.body: At the common fixed-flow, fixed-head acceptance basis the energies order as P2 12, P3 52, P1 56, P4 58 kWh per run. Gaps from the leader: 40 kWh to P3, 44 to P1, 46 to P4. The three followers cluster within 6 kWh of one another, while P2 is an extreme outlier on the low side. Because all modules were tested on the identical duty, these differences are directly comparable and are not measurement artifacts of differing test conditions. No tie occurs, so the candidate-ID tie-break is never exercised.
sections.heading: Verified Energy Ranking and Gap Arithmetic

sections.body: I checked the proposal's claims one by one. Its eligibility table, quality values, defect counts, energy values, ranking, gap arithmetic (40/44/46 kWh) and the note that P3 is exactly at the threshold all match the trusted table. Its statement that defect counts gate eligibility but do not re-rank qualifying modules is correct policy reading. One element is a judgment rather than policy: the proposal frames P4 as a 'managed fallback' should P2's defect prove systemic. The policy defines no fallback mechanism, so this is reasonable planning language, not a binding rule, and it does not alter the award. I found no factual errors in A.
sections.heading: Audit of the Delivered Proposal Report

sections.body: Several items remain open and must stay separate from verified facts. First, raw defect counts say nothing about defect type, severity, location or repair status; P2's single defect is uncharacterized. Second, the trusted comparison rests on one acceptance run at one fixed duty, so behavior across other duties or duty cycles is untested. Third, cost, delivery schedule, maintenance burden and field reliability are unverified for every candidate. Any new evidence must be re-tested against the same gates and basis before it can change the award. Until then, the verified record stands: P2 wins on energy.
